Hospital Knowledge Base — Complete
Reference Manual
Comprehensive operational, clinical, triage, and patient safety protocols.
Admission Protocols & Procedures
1. Patient Identification & Registration
  Verify identity using at least two unique identifiers (Full Name, Date of Birth, Medical Record Number).
 Issue standard hospital identification band immediately upon verification.
 Review and document insurance coverage, emergency contact details, and advance directives.
2. Bed Allocation & Workflow
  Emergency Intake: Direct transfer from Triage/ED following clinical stabilization.
 Elective Admissions: Pre-registration completed 24–48 hours prior to scheduled procedures.
 Coordinate with Central Bed Management to assign beds based on clinical acuity (ICU, Step-Down, General
Ward).
3. Clinical Handover & Medication Reconciliation
  Complete baseline vital signs and nursing intake assessment within 60 minutes of ward arrival.

3. Clinical Handover & Medication Reconciliation
  Complete baseline vital signs and nursing intake assessment within 60 minutes of ward arrival.
 Perform structured medication reconciliation documenting current home medications, dosages, and drug
allergies.
Hospital Departments & Functional Overview
Emergency Department (ED)
  Responsibilities: 24/7 acute resuscitation, trauma intake, rapid triage.
 Contacts: ED Triage Desk, On-call Attending.
Inpatient Wards
  Responsibilities: General medicine, surgical post-op recovery, care planning.
 Contacts: Ward Charge Nurse, Resident on Duty.
Intensive Care Unit (ICU)
  Responsibilities: Critical care, invasive mechanical ventilation, continuous hemodynamic monitoring.
 Contacts: Attending Intensivist.
Surgical Services (OR)
  Responsibilities: Elective & emergency procedures, PACU recovery.
 Contacts: OR Coordinator, Anesthesiology Lead.

Diagnostic Radiology
  Responsibilities: X-Ray, CT, MRI, Ultrasound diagnostics.
 Contacts: Radiology Control Desk.
Pathology & Clinical Lab
  Responsibilities: Hematology, biochemistry, blood bank cross-matching.
 Contacts: Central Laboratory Lead.
Pharmacy Services
  Responsibilities: Inpatient dispensing, IV sterile compounding, clinical review.
 Contacts: Inpatient Pharmacy Specialist.
Emergency Response & Critical Protocols
1. Standard Emergency Codes
  Code Blue: Cardiac or respiratory arrest. Call dedicated internal emergency extension; deploy crash cart and
code team immediately.
 Code Red: Fire or smoke detection. Execute R.A.C.E. (Rescue, Alarm, Contain, Extinguish/Evacuate).
 Code Black: Bomb threat or suspicious unattended package. Alert Security immediately; avoid handheld radio
transmissions nearby.
 Code Silver: Active shooter or armed threat. Follow Run, Hide, Fight procedures.

 Code Silver: Active shooter or armed threat. Follow Run, Hide, Fight procedures.
 Code Orange: External disaster or mass casualty event. Activate Hospital Incident Command System (HICS).
2. Emergency Severity Index (ESI) Triage
  1. Level 1 (Resuscitation): Immediate life-saving intervention required (cardiac arrest, severe shock, airway
compromise).
 2. Level 2 (Emergent): High-risk, altered mental status, severe respiratory distress, or severe pain.
 3. Level 3 (Urgent): Stable vitals requiring two or more diagnostic/therapeutic resources.
 4. Level 4 (Less Urgent): Requires one simple diagnostic/treatment resource (e.g., single X-ray, minor
sutures).
 5. Level 5 (Non-Urgent): Requires zero clinical resources (e.g., medication refill, basic consultation).
Hospital General Operations & Governance
1. Operational Overview & Mission
  Dedicated to evidence-based, compassionate, patient-centered inpatient and outpatient care.

1. Operational Overview & Mission
  Dedicated to evidence-based, compassionate, patient-centered inpatient and outpatient care.
 Governance overseen by the Executive Board, Chief Medical Officer, and Nursing Leadership Council.
2. Facility Security & Access Guidelines
  General Visiting Hours: 10:00 AM – 8:00 PM daily (maximum 2 visitors per bedside).
 Restricted Care Units (ICU/NICU): Restricted visiting schedules; immediate family members only.

 Security Checkpoints: Mandatory keycard badge access for Operating Theatres, Central Pharmacy, Nursery,
and Biohazard storage.
3. Regulatory Compliance & Accreditation
  Continuous compliance with healthcare quality commissions and environmental safety audits.
 Strict enforcement of patient data confidentiality under HIPAA and national medical privacy regulations.
Patient Safety & Quality Protocols
1. Fall Prevention Protocols
  Administer Morse Fall Scale assessment on admission and at every shift handover.
 Implement precautions for high-risk patients: yellow identification band, non-skid socks, bed rails raised, bed
alarm enabled.
2. Medication Safety (ISMP Standards)
  Apply the 5 Rights of Medication Administration: Right Patient, Right Drug, Right Dose, Right Route, Right
Time.
 Mandatory independent double-check for high-alert medications (e.g., Insulin, IV Heparin infusions,
Concentrated Electrolytes).

3. Infection Prevention & Control
  Strict adherence to the WHO 5 Moments of Hand Hygiene.
 Maintain appropriate Isolation Precautions (Contact, Droplet, Airborne) and verify required PPE before room
entry.
4. Universal Protocol (Surgical & Invasive Procedures)
  Pre-procedure verification of patient, site, and procedure.
 Site marking performed by the operating practitioner.
 Mandatory bedside "Time-Out" conducted by the entire clinical team immediately prior to incision.
